For in gold we can take wisdom; in silver, eloquence; in blue silk, heavenly conversation; in purple, the shedding of blood through martyrdom. For then we fruitfully gather these riches, when we find them acceptable in right faith, if we transfer this victory to the spiritual enemies. Then we ought to be secure, when after the end of the present life there is no need to fear the snares of enemies. For then we gather the spoils wholesomely, when we shall receive from Christ the worthy rewards of our labor. Whence it is well said that Judas exhorted his men not to covet the spoils while the cruel wars of the enemies were threatening; when the enemies had been utterly overcome, then he returned with his men to gather the spoils of the camp, because it is necessary that every preacher admonish his hearers to guard against the darts of enemies as long as it is the time of war. But when the time of peace itself has come, namely the peace which the Saviour promised his disciples, saying: “My peace I give unto you,” then prelates and subjects alike will have eternal joy from the promised reward, because they will no longer fear the sorrow that follows of labors and tears, for then it is the time to sing praises to God their helper. Whence it is written:
52_marg3775: And turning they sang a hymn, etc. Salvation is greater in Israel when the number of believers is multiplied in the Lord from the peoples; who acknowledge the Saviour by faith, confess him with the mouth, and glorify him in good work. Or otherwise, then there will be greater salvation in Israel, when there will be no adversity in the Church of Christ. And it is significantly added, “in that day”: namely the day of the resurrection, when the most noble bride will be joined in the heavenly kingdom above to the bridegroom, when all the saints in the sight of God will rejoice not only in the rest of their souls but also in the immortality of their bodies.
52_marg3776: Whosoever of the aliens, etc. Finally the aliens, escaping, announce the victory of Judas to Lysias; for those who are not taken as most saving prey of Christ through the ministry of the holy doctors announce the glory of Christ, though unwilling, being constrained by the truth, to their masters, by whom they are nourished unto death. For Lysias, which is interpreted “generating,” signifies the powerful of the world, who, though they have been begotten, have not yet deserved to be begotten by the baptism of Christ. These therefore, hearing the victory of the soldiers of Christ, are amazed and discouraged in mind, because things did not succeed in Israel such as they wished, and as the king commanded. For their will was this: that the preaching of the Gospel through the holy doctors should not prevail, nor the multitude of those believing in the Lord be increased. And they knew that such things pleased their rulers also, that is, the unclean spirits; for, venerated by men with divine worship in the profane images of idols, they persuaded them of this, that they should not receive the faith of Christ; but they did not prevail, because the Father made manifest the glory of his Son far and wide among all nations.
52_marg3777: And the year following, etc. And Lysias chose sixty thousand men and five thousand horsemen to fight against Israel; so with all the time of this world, which is divided into six ages, through the five bodily senses the prince of this world, the rulers of these darkness urging him on, strives to overcome the soldiers of Christ by tearing them with various vices, and through wicked men he plots the death of the good. But Judas meets them with ten thousand men, because the army of our king is in this stronger than the rest: that in all things it is eager to obey the divine precepts, and sending constant prayers to the Lord it is strengthened by the hand of him in whose power it chiefly trusts, and it keeps on in the battle until its enemies and the adverse band are utterly slain by the spiritual sword; whence it is added in the prayer of Judas.
52_marg3778: Cast them down, etc. There are five books of the law of God, and there are five senses, as we said before, the bodily ones. For he who according to the teaching of the law restrains the concupiscence of the flesh, “turning away his eyes that they may not behold vanity,” “stopping his ears that they may not” hear the detracting tongue, and obscene songs for worldly uses, by hearing which frequently the inner man is defiled; he who holds back his smell and taste, lest he make use of the allurement of pleasures; “who refrains his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile, turns away from evil and does good, seeks peace and pursues it”—this man, overcoming his enemies, shall take a most saving victory, and shall rejoice in the most abundant triumph. But the spiritual Lysias, though once, twice and thrice crushed he has taken to flight, yet does not desist from the wickedness begun, but again raises up renewed battles. Whence it is written:
52_marg3779: And Lysias seeing, etc. It is well said that Judas, the enemies being crushed and the wars lulled for a time, exhorts his men to cleanse; for the holy doctors have the greatest zeal that, in whatever respects the Church of those subject to them has been hurt by enemies, it may again be restored to its former state of holy conversation. According to the tropological sense, moreover, it is necessary that each of the faithful, if anything in his mind has been defiled by the fraud of the enemy—and that mind we can well take as designated by the name of mount Sion, because Sion is interpreted a watch-tower; and “blessed are the clean of heart, for they shall see God”—should purge what has been done with an urgent gaze, until it is renewed to the full. For there we can understand the sanctification deserted, and the altar profaned, and the gates burnt; for there the sacrifice of praise was offered to God on the altar of faith, and the entrance of the heavenly life was meditated. In the courts, moreover, shrubs grow up when in human hearts the growth of superfluous thoughts is generated. “The chambers,” it says, “they saw thrown down.” The pastophoria are called in Greek thalami, or bedchambers, in which the Levites kept watch in the courts of the house of the Lord, of which mention is made in the last vision of the prophet Ezechiel. The chambers therefore are thrown down when the secrets of the mind are torn to pieces by unlawful desires. But all these things most of all need to be purified most earnestly by penance for sins, and amendment of morals, and pious prayers to the Lord. Whence it is rightly written of the army of Judas that when they saw the sanctuary desolate, “they rent their garments, and made great lamentation,” etc.
52_marg3780: Then Judas appointed men, etc. It is aptly said that Judas appointed men to fight against them that were in the castle, till they had cleansed the holy places; for this our Redeemer appoints through his preachers, that his soldiers may earnestly fight against those who dwell in the castle of pride, that is, men puffed up with the spirit of conceit, or also the malignant spirits swelling with pride, until they purge the hearts of the elect from every stain of iniquity. “And he chose priests without blemish, whose will was set upon the law of God, and they cleansed the holy places”; for, having cast out from ecclesiastical office those who had in themselves the leprosy of error or the stain of crimes, he chose as ministers of the word men willing and approved in morals in the faith of God, that he might make the assemblies of the holy Church free from all contagion of error. Therefore it is added that he “took away the stones that had been defiled into an unclean place”; because heretics, who wished through the conversation of right faith and sound doctrine to become precious stones, he anathematized, smitten and cast out from the communion of the Church, and made it plain to all that they were reprobate.
52_marg3781: And he considered, etc. The altar of holocausts is the pure faith, right doctrine, and clean conduct of Christ’s ministers. But if this altar has been profaned by heretical perversity or by the enormity of crimes, it will now have to be destroyed, that is, to be deposed from the dignity of the priesthood, lest perhaps it be a reproach to holy Church that she has perverse and wicked teachers, who have been led astray by the cunning of the devil. Whence the Lord says in the Gospel to his disciples: “You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt lose its savour, wherewith shall it be salted? It is good for nothing any more but to be cast out, and to be trodden on by men.” Of this Paul also, writing to Titus, says: “A man that is a heretic, after the first and second admonition, avoid: knowing that he, that is such an one, is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned by his own judgment.” Hence he also says to certain offenders: “By you the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles.” So, then, when the mystical altar has been put down, these stones ought to be laid up in the mountain of the house in a fitting place, until the prophet comes and gives answer, saying: that sinners ought to be brought under penance, until by holy teachers it is judged what fitting satisfaction has been made for the crime committed. But in their place whole stones ought to be put, according to the law, that a new altar may be made like the former one: because men sound in the catholic faith, instructed in the knowledge of the holy scriptures, and religious in good morals, ought to be put in the place of government from which the transgressors have fallen, according to the authorities of the divine law, so that without reproach, in newness of life and by the rule of justice, service may be rendered to God in the holy Church, which Christ acquired for himself by the price of his blood as a bride “not having spot or wrinkle.”
52_marg3782: And they built the holy places, etc. Holy preachers build the holy places within the house, inside, and the temple, when they adorn the people subject to them within by the knowledge of the sound faith, and without by honest conduct. They sanctify the courts when they dedicate those newly coming to the faith by instructing them in the divine sacraments. They make new holy vessels when they make the hearts of men fit for receiving the word of God. They bring in the candlestick, and the altar of incense, and the table into the temple, when they raise up in the Church of God the light of spiritual doctrine, the purity of holy working, and the meditation of the holy scriptures. In the candlestick, then, on which the lamps ought to shine, we can rightly see the discourse of evangelical doctrine, on which holy teachers, kindled with the fire of the Holy Spirit, ought to shine, that those who enter may see the light. Whence the Truth himself says in the Gospel: “Neither do men light a candle and put it under a bushel, but upon a candlestick, that it may shine to all that are in the house.” By the altar of incense we can understand nothing better than the perfect life of the saints, whence daily the odour of virtues and of holy prayer is fragrant in the sight of the Most High. The table of the Lord, then, we understand to be none other than the sacred scripture, in which the refreshment of souls consists. But as to what is said, that they hung up the veils and finished all the works that they had made: in the hanging of the veils the hiding of the mysteries is expressed. For the mysteries of the divine law are not all to be laid open to all, but according to the capacity of each one’s mind and the progress of knowledge and of virtues. Whence the Lord commands the apostles, saying: “Give not that which is holy to dogs; neither cast ye your pearls before swine.” And Paul says to untaught disciples: “I gave you milk to drink, not meat; for you were not able as yet; but neither indeed are you now able.” Of the knowledge of the perfect, then, he says elsewhere: “But we all, beholding the glory of the Lord with open face, are transformed into the same image, as by the Spirit of the Lord,” etc. They finish, then, all the works that are to be done in the house of God, who strive in faith, speech and work to fulfil in order all the commandments of the Lord; and nothing is lacking in perfection where the human will in all things obeys the divine will.
52_marg3783: And before morning, etc. Of this renewal Josephus thus tells, saying: On the twenty-fifth day of the month Casleu, which the Macedonians call Appelleon, they lighted the lamps upon the candlestick, and burned the holocausts which they offered on the new altar. These things were done after three years, on the same day on which their religion had been changed to the profane custom of idols. For the temple, destroyed by Antiochus, so remained for three years. For in the hundred and forty-fifth year these things were done in the temple, on the twenty-fifth day of the month Appelleus, in the hundred and fifty-third Olympiad. But it was renewed on the same day, the twenty-fifth of the month Appelleus, in the hundred and forty-eighth year, in the hundred and fifty-fourth Olympiad. The desolation of the temple happened according to the foretelling of Daniel, which he had foretold four hundred and eight years before, by which he signified that the Macedonians would destroy it. And Judas with his citizens celebrated sacrifices for the renewal of the temple for eight days, leaving out no kind of delight, but feeding them with the most costly feasts; and he glorified God with praises and psalms, and they delighted one another with songs. For the renewal of the solemnities, after a mutual interval, religion being inspired, the receivers of the law decreed that their posterity should celebrate this renewal of the temple for eight days. Whence from that time until now we celebrate this feast, calling it Lights, because beyond hope this splendid light of the religion to be cherished appeared to us. Mystically, however, the renewal of the temple is the conversion of men to penance for sins, who had been defiled by some errors and crimes. For then all the faithful ought to sing, rejoice, be glad, shout for joy and praise, when they see their neighbours, by the amendment of their morals and by meditation on the law of God, restoring in themselves what they had before let fall through negligence. Whence the holy Gospel also tells that the Saviour said that joy is born in heaven over one sinner doing penance. If over one, how much more will there be exultation over many converted to the true worship of God. For as it is written: “In the multitude of the people is the dignity of the king”; of that prince, namely, who “will have all men to be saved, and to come to the knowledge of the truth.”
52_marg3784: And Judas decreed, etc. The Saviour himself is read in the Gospel to have adorned this solemnity by his preaching, where it is written: “And it was the feast of the dedication at Jerusalem, and it was winter. And Jesus walked in the temple, in Solomon’s porch,” etc. Whence it is to be known that this dedication, which we learn was held according to the Gospel reading, belongs not to the first dedication of the temple but to the last. This is easily gathered from the fact that it is reported as held in winter. For its first dedication was made by Solomon in the time of autumn; the middle one by Zorobabel and Jesus the priest, in the time of spring; the last by Judas Machabeus in the time of winter, when it is read that it was specially ordained that the same dedication should be recalled in memory every year with solemn services, according to which, as we have learned from the aforesaid saying of the Gospel, it was observed until the time of the Lord’s incarnation. This, however, was concerning the second and third dedication. For Solomon finished in seven years the work of the temple which he built for the Lord, and in the eighth year, on the tenth day of the seventh month, which is called by us October, he dedicated it in great glory. But after four hundred and thirty years the Chaldeans burned this temple, and, the city of Jerusalem being destroyed, led the people of Israel away captive into Babylon; who after seventy years, the Persians reigning, were sent back to their country, and the temple was built again through forty-six years, and on the third day of the twelfth month, which we call March, the work was brought to its end. Over this work then were set the most valiant leaders of the people, as we have said, Zorobabel of the royal race, and Jesus, the high priest, and also the prophets Aggeus and Zacharias helping them and strengthening the heart of the people against the plots of the enemies who hindered the work. Then after almost three hundred and fifty years, the most wicked king of the Greeks, Antiochus, having taken Jerusalem by fraud, profaned the same temple with the filth of idols, taking away from it and breaking the golden altar of the Lord, the table of proposition, the candlestick of light, and the other things which were mentioned above. But Judas Machabeus also, since he was of the priestly race, having gathered an army of the just, taking up arms against the captains of Antiochus and driving them out of Judea, put an end to the most cruel persecution, and cleansing the temple of the images of the idols, making new altars again and the other vessels and ornaments and placing them in the temple, dedicated them together with the temple. This he purified and renewed on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month, which is called by us December, and that this belongs to winter is doubted by no one. And he established a decree, as we said before, that every year the day of the encenia, that is, of the renewal and dedication of the temple, should be celebrated with festal devotion, as this place now testifies. All which things, as the apostle teaches, “were done in a figure of us,” and were certainly written on our account, and therefore are to be discussed by us more carefully by spiritual reasoning. For king Solomon, which is interpreted peaceable, typically designates our Redeemer himself; of whom Isaias says: “His empire shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end of peace.” The temple which he built is his catholic Church, which he gathers together from all who believe throughout the world, as from living stones, into one structure of his faith and charity. But that the temple was built in seven years signifies that through the whole time of this world, which is run through in seven days, the structure of the holy Church never ceases to grow. That it was dedicated in the eighth year, and that most celebrated and greatest solemnity was shown by king Solomon to all the children of Israel at the time of the completed dedication, hints mystically that, when the number of the elect is complete at the end of the world, the festival of the long-desired immortality will follow, and, the miracle of the universal resurrection having been accomplished, all who belong to the kingdom of the true peaceable king, that is, Solomon, will soon enter with him the eternal joys of the heavenly country. For since our Lord willed to be raised from death on the eighth day, that is, after the seventh of the sabbath, the number eight rightly designates also the coming feasts of our resurrection. That the temple burned by enemies is built again by the Lord’s mercy, and that what was defiled by idolaters is cleansed anew by the help of heavenly goodness, hints at the various events of the holy Church, which is now oppressed by the persecution of unbelievers, now, restored to greater freedom by the persecutors, serves the Lord in quiet servitude; now in some of her members she is endangered by the plots of the ancient enemy, now by the pressing diligence of faithful teachers she receives back, already chastened through penance, those whom he seemed for a time to destroy. But that the temple was built a second time in forty-six years looks spiritually to the signification of the Lord’s body, which he took of the Virgin. Of which he himself says to the Jews: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up,” because he himself raised on the third day to life his body loosed by the passion. For the natural philosophers say that the body of man is formed in the distinction of its members on the forty-sixth day after the beginning of conception, and therefore it was not by chance but divinely arranged that the temple should be built in that number of years in which number of days the Lord’s body, which was figured by the temple, had to be perfected in the virginal womb. But that it was ordained to celebrate the encenia every year, this certainly admonishes us, ever keeping in mind the memory of the Lord’s resurrection, which we believe already accomplished, and hoping for our own future resurrection, so to act that we may deserve to rise not to judgment but, as the Lord promised to those who have done good things, to life.
52_marg3785: And they built at that time. The holy doctors build mount Sion when they stir up holy Church by word and example to advance in virtues. They build high walls round about when they fortify her on every side with the care of the catholic faith and with the work of prayers. They raise strong towers when they teach men to place all their hope in the goodness of God. Lest the Gentiles should at any time tread it down as they did before: that is, that the wickedness of malignant spirits, or the malice of perverse men, may not prevail any longer to harm them. And he placed there, it says, a garrison to keep it. A garrison is placed in Sion to keep it when a throng of ministers is provided in the Church for the observance of the law of God and the rite of the heavenly sacraments. They fortify it to secure Bethsura when by strong exhortations they urge churchmen to keep the divine worship according to rule. For Bethsura is interpreted the house of the strong. That the people might have a defence against Idumea, that is, that it may keep constancy of faith against enemies and against the obstinacy of a raging world.
52_marg3786: And it came to pass, etc. The Gentiles are provoked when they see the work of the worship of God renewed, because both invisible enemies, and visible ones too, who pant with the heats of envy against the progress of faith and virtues, are angered, and torment and persecute the servants of God, wishing to bring them to nothing, when they see that they wish to restore the observance of good works upon the altar of right faith. Hence it is said that they thought to destroy the generation of Jacob that were among them, and they began to kill them, because as the gospel of Christ grew bright in the world, and men received the faith of God, the persecutors were tormented, and by treating them with punishments strove to turn them away from it. Likewise also the spiritual enemies, when they see some who, out of the sloth of negligence, wish to be restored in the worship of piety, strive to kill them with the sword of impiety and to slay them with the death of sins. But Judas, resisting the enemies bravely with the shield of faith, overcomes the children of Esau in Idumea, because with the choirs of holy doctors, slaying with the sword of the spirit the idolaters, who are roughest with the thorn-thickets of vices and most foul with deadly sacrifices and worldly luxury, he makes subjects of adversaries and friends of enemies.
52_marg3787: And those who were, etc. Those who dwelt in the places mentioned, that is, Agrabathane and Bean, and who, besieging the children of Israel, became a snare and a stumbling-block, lying in wait for them, signify the Jews and heretics, who are always devising scandals and snares against the Church of God. But such men are shut up by Judas and his companions in their towers, when they are caught in the machinations of their pride by the diligence of the doctors, and their errors are anathematized; and their towers are burnt with fire with all that are in them, when the authors of crimes and inventors of errors, for their sins, are both now consumed by the ardour of the divine word, and in the future judgment, unless they have first done fitting penance, will be burnt up with the fire of everlasting vengeance.
52_marg3788: And he passed over, etc. What is expressed by the children of Ammon, which is interpreted son of my people, if not schismatics and heretics, who once seemed to be sons of holy Church, but withdrawing from it and casting themselves into error, became sons of the devil? Whence John the apostle says: “They went out from us, but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would no doubt have remained with us.” These have Timotheus for leader, that is, heresiarchs, who according to the interpretation of their name are praised among them, but according to the truth of understanding are found among us to be wicked. For Timotheus is interpreted beneficent. But this opinion of the heresiarchs is among the deceived; among us they are rather called poisoners than benefactors, because with their evil deeds they mix the poison of error for their hearers. Against them Judas rising up and proving superior takes the victory, and by destroying their errors returns into Judea, that is, into the confession of the praise of God, with the triumph over the enemies.
52_marg3789: And were gathered together, etc. The Gentiles that are in Galaad gather together against the Israelites to destroy them, when a multitude of heretics and schismatics comes together to this end, that by the testimonies of the scriptures perverted according to their own sense they may assail the catholic faith, which is in holy Church. For Galaad is interpreted heap of testimony, a name that fits well those who devote themselves to meditation on the scriptures. But the Israelites flee into the fortress, when all the faithful take refuge in the truth of the faith; and they ask that help be brought them by Judas and his brethren, because through the ministries of holy preachers they long to be defended by the gospel of Christ against the spiritual Timotheus, of whom we have spoken above, and his companions. And that the Israelites complain of the killing and captivity of their own shows that there is no small groaning among the faithful when they see some of their own depart from the truth and fall into the error of the perverse.
52_marg3790: And behold others, etc. Those strangers who came together from various places to destroy the people of God clearly designate the peoples of the Gentiles, who, while they are still in unbelief, stir up wars and persecutions against Christians. But when the words were heard which the various embassies brought to Judas and his companions, a great assembly met together to consider what they should do for their brethren that were in trouble and were assaulted by enemies, because the solicitude and care of the whole holy Church is very great as to how she may defend her sons against various enemies, that is, Jews, pagans, heretics and schismatics. This too she does with prudent counsel and with entire attention, with those who seem more learned and stronger in faith and the work of virtues, so that she may resist the enemies and defend her own in due season.
52_marg3791: And Judas said. As the assaults of the enemies upon the Church are diverse, so the battles of the spiritual warriors ought to be distinct. Simon is sent into Galilee with three thousand men, as is shown in what follows, to deliver his brethren. But Judas and Jonathan go into Galaad with eight thousand. And what is signified by Simon, who is sent into Galilee, that is, a wheel, but preachers sent to the nations? They, preparing to go against their adversaries with three thousand, that is, with faith in the holy Trinity, strive by gospel preaching to cast down the enemies and to deliver believers. But Judas and Jonathan represent those teachers who, preaching the word of God in Judea, strive to overcome by the truth of a sound understanding both Jews and also heretics who misuse the testimonies of the Scriptures. And it is not that Simon alone is sent with his men against the Gentiles, while against the Jews and heretics two undertake to go with more; for among the Gentiles only idolatry with pagan error had to be overcome, whereas among the Jews and heretics partly old custom, partly new superstition had to be corrected by the spiritual knowledge of the two testaments. Where eight thousand men are taken, because there it is taught that either the circumcision of the law is to be spiritually observed or the resurrection of Christ is truly to be believed.
52_marg3792: And Simon went, etc. Simon fights many battles with the Gentiles, as the holy preachers throughout the whole world strive to overcome idolatry and the confused errors of the Gentiles. “The heathens were discomfited before his face,” when they lay aside their obstinacy in resisting the Gospel of God. “He pursued them even to the gate of Ptolemais,” when they are taken in their own inventions, with which they contrived by vain pursuits to contradict the word of God, overcome by the truth itself, and are subjected by the confession of the right faith. Whence it is fittingly added: “And there fell of the heathens almost three thousand men.” These, falling from the wicked state of pride into the penance of sins, rising the better through right faith, deserve to be raised up into a state of good works. Simon takes their spoils, when the catholic teacher strives to turn to the service of God whatever they have laboured at in knowledge of letters or the search for truth. Whence very many of those who had been trained in the liberal arts in Gentile life, converted to catholic doctrine, shone most gloriously. But those who were in Galilee, with their wives and children and all that was theirs, he brought into Judea with great joy, when, drawing out from there any catholics entangled in the affairs of the world by the doctrine of the Gospel, he teaches them to seek the things that are of God with all care and all effort.
52_marg3793: And Judas Machabeus, etc. Against those who held the captive Jews in Galaad, Judas Machabeus and his brother Jonathan with their companions were sent, “passed over the Jordan, and went three days’ journey through the desert.” So the holy preachers, sent into the world to call men to the faith of Christ and to overthrow Jewish and schismatic errors, first pass over the Jordan, when they teach that one must first pass by the sacrament of baptism from the darkness of unbelief into the grace of Christ, the truth itself attesting that “unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Ghost, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.” Then they go a three days’ journey through the desert, because they affirm that the faith of the holy Trinity, which all the faithful profess in baptism, is to be observed with good works throughout the whole time of dwelling in this world. But that the Nabutheans met him peaceably and told what had befallen the brethren in Galaad signifies that the sayings of the holy prophets bring opportune comfort to the holy teachers, when by their attestation they make manifest all the torments that those who believe in Christ are to suffer. For Nabutheans means prophesying, and by true prophecy they foretell the errors which the sons of perdition contrive to set against the truth of the Gospel of Christ. Whence Osee pursues the cows of Bethaven and the inhabitants of Samaria, and Amos reproaches the praise of those sacrificing of leaven, and also detests those “that turn judgment into wormwood,” and receive a gift and oppress the poor in the gate. But when the Nabutheans report that some of the Jews were shut up in Barasa and Bosor, the interpretation of their name well expresses the effect of the matter. For Barasa and Bosor are interpreted tribulations or distress, because all, according to the voice of Paul, who will live godly in Christ suffer persecution, nor will he escape the injury of heretics who strives to keep the doctrine of the sound faith. These John the apostle in his Apocalypse describes as inflicting torment, like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a man; because as scorpions carry their poison in the tail, so heretics hide the malice in the completion of their fraud, that they may harm the unwary the more, not with open face but by lurking snares.
52_marg3794: And Judas turned. Above he tells that the cities of Galaad, in which the Jews were shut up, were fortified and great, which Judas determined to take and destroy in one day, because through unity the holy preachers purpose to destroy all the fortifications of false doctrines which heretics set up to deceive the souls of the innocent and to make them captive by their errors. But now he says that Judas in the desert of Bosor took the city of Bosor, and slew every male with the edge of the sword, and took their spoils, and burnt it with fire; because the holy teachers strive earnestly for this: that, having taken the stronghold of the heretics, they may destroy by the sword of the Holy Spirit, which is the word of God, all the strength of the wicked sects which they set up by the philosophy of the world and vain deceit; so that what those feigned by their display to be outstanding, these may show to be trifles and frivolous. They take their spoils, when they take away from them, as from unjust possessors, the testimonies of the holy Scriptures which they have abused, and burn the very composition with perpetual anathema. But what follows, that they rose up from there by night, shows that they were left in the darkness of their error.
52_marg3795: And it came to pass at daybreak, etc. What is expressed by the ladders and engines of the Gentiles, if not the exaltation and obstinacy of the proud, by which they desire to overthrow and subvert the Church of Christ? But our Judas, who sets the whole apparatus of war in the light, fights against them in three companies, that is, with the faith of the holy Trinity, or with a threefold doctrine, that is, the historical, the allegorical, and the tropological. And he cries out with trumpets to heaven, because by strong preaching he raises his voice, and with the inmost cry of the heart he calls upon God as helper in prayer.
52_marg3796: And they knew, etc. The camp of Timothy: when Machabeus was known, they fled from his face, because heretics, when the power and truth of our Lord Jesus Christ are recognized, flee terrified. And they are struck with a great plague, because in them the vengeance of anathema is exercised according to justice through the holy teachers; and there fall of them almost eight thousand men, since every heap of errors, by which they strove to oppose the true understanding of the spiritual circumcision, or the faith of the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ and of his members, is destroyed by the truth itself prevailing. Hence it is that the Saviour in the Gospel, loosing the typical sabbath, made known to us the sacrament of his resurrection on the first of the sabbath, which is also the eighth day after the seventh. Hence also the apostle Paul teaches that the circumcision “not made by hand, in despoiling of the body of the flesh,” ought to be wrought not in the body but by the Spirit of the living God in the hearts of believers. Whence also the old law taught that the foreskin of the heart is to be circumcised.
52_marg3797: But after this. After Timothy had been conquered once and again, he did not cease to increase wickedness, but multiplied malice. Again he raises an army against Judas and his companions, because it is not enough for heretics to carry on contentions once and again in small number, but they always stir up new wars against the Church, and pour out the manifold poisons of their perfidy. They pitch camp against Raphon, beyond the torrent, because with the utmost effort they stir up the fury of their pride and raise the storm of wars; and they also bring in the Arabians, which is interpreted “of the plains,” as auxiliaries, because they take as help for their error the voluptuous, who follow the luxury of this world. Whence also the Jovinianists built up no small wickedness of their error against the Church. But Judas sends men to spy out their army, when the holy teachers warn their hearers to guard against the tumult of the wicked, lest they bring the work of their fraud to the destruction of simple souls. And that Timothy, as if making a gathering, says to the captains of his army: “When Judas and his army come near the torrent of water, if he pass over unto us first, we shall not be able to withstand him: for he will certainly prevail over us. But if he be afraid to pass over, and camp on the other side of the river, we will pass over to them and shall prevail against him.” This shows that all heretics greatly fear the confidence and constancy of the rightly believing people, and acknowledge themselves the weaker the stronger they see those people in the unity of faith. But if they have seen any of the Catholics becoming slower in meditation on the law of God and in the exercise of good works, they promise themselves with rejoicing the triumph over them and their captivity.
52_marg3798: And when he came near, etc. Judas, passing over the torrent of water, set scribes of the people to exhort the multitude after him to go to battle, as our Redeemer, going to the passion of the cross, appointed the apostles, that they might teach those who believe in him to despise the torment of bodily death and to trust in the power of heavenly strength. Whence is that which in the Gospel he commanded the disciples, saying: “When you shall hear of wars and seditions, be not terrified.” And again: “Fear ye not them that kill the body, and are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him that can destroy both soul and body in hell.” And again: “In your patience,” he says, “you shall possess your souls. But he that shall persevere to the end, he shall be saved.” And elsewhere: “Blessed,” he says, “are they that suffer persecution for justice’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” Hence it is well added: he passed over to them first, and all the people after him, because it was fitting that the mediator of God and men should first fulfil the mystery of his passion, and so, strengthened by his example, the faithful from all nations should rightly learn, in suffering for him, to despise death. And all the nations were broken before their face, when the various errors of men are crushed by the power of the virtue of God. They threw away their arms and fled to the temple which is in Carnaim. When the hindrances of their contentions have been abandoned, the persecutors of the truth, not daring to resist, hiding themselves in the shrines of their errors, seek protection from the very place whence they have their ruin. Now Carnaim is interpreted “horns.” Horns can aptly be taken for kingdom and defence. But their opinion did not help them; rather it deceived them, because Judas took the city itself and burnt the temple with fire with all things that were in it, when our Saviour not only destroys every contrivance of the errors of heretics and persecutors, but also burns with the fire of just vengeance all who trust in it. Whence the Lord commanded in Deuteronomy, saying: If you shall hear in one of your cities, which the Lord your God shall give you to dwell in, some saying: “Children of Belial are gone out of the midst of thee, and have withdrawn the inhabitants of their city, and have said: Let us go, and serve strange gods which you know not.” Inquire carefully and diligently, the truth of the matter being looked into, and if you find it certain that what is said is so, and that this abomination has been committed in deed, you shall immediately strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, and shall destroy it and all that is in it, even to the cattle. And whatever household goods there are, you shall gather together in the midst of its streets, and burn them with the city itself, so as to consume all for the Lord your God, and that it be a heap for ever.
52_marg3799: And Judas gathered together, etc. Judas gathers the Israelites from Galaad, when our Redeemer through his teachers calls back by the word of the Gospel to the Catholic faith those who have been taken captive by heretics; for this is to come into the land of Juda: to praise God with right faith and good works.
52_marg3800: And they came as far as Ephron, etc. The various battles of the nations signify the various wars of vices and errors. We have said that those nations that were in the land of Galaad and strove to take the Israelites captive signify heretics and Jews; but now, these having been overcome who were in Carnaim, again those who were in Ephron endeavour to resist Judas and his companions, because, the various heretics having been crushed, those who still follow the letter of the Old Testament are unwilling to open the way of spiritual understanding. For what is signified by Ephron, which is interpreted “dust of sorrow” or “useless dust,” if not the superfluous observance of the law in the times of grace, in which the Jews, trusting, shut themselves in and block the gates with stones; who, given over to the shadow, set the historical tradition of the law, which was written on stones, against the preachers of the Gospel, and do not consent to be torn from it in any way, nor allow others to follow a more right sense. Whence the Truth itself says to such in the Gospel: “Woe to you lawyers, for you have taken away the key of knowledge: you yourselves have not entered in, and those that were entering in, you have hindered.” But Judas sends to them with words of peace, saying: “Let us pass through your land, to go into our country: and no man shall hurt you.” Because the holy preachers, according to the Lord’s command, first offer peace to the opposing party, that what is written may be fulfilled: “And if the son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon him; but if not, it shall return to you.” “We will pass through,” they say, “your land, to go into our country.” As if they said: let us read the history of your books, that there, in the allegorical sense, we may find the country promised to us in heaven. “And no man shall hurt you,” because our passing will be harmless to you. “We will only pass through on foot,” when by the step of good works we desire to approach the kingdom above. “They would not open” – when, in the law handed down to them, they were unwilling to have fellowship with the preachers of the Gospel.
52_marg3801: And Judas commanded. What is it that Judas commanded to proclaim in the camp that each one should draw near to the city in the place where he was, if not that the holy teachers grant their hearers free understanding in the sacred Scriptures, so that each one, what he seeks to have opened to him in the divine reading, whether by allegory, or by tropology, or by anagoge, according to the wish of his desire, may, the grace from above consenting, receive the power of entering. And not that the men of valour are said to draw near there and to assault the city all that day and all that night. Because unless one is a man of valour, so as to desire to fulfil in deed what he has learned by the tradition of his masters, and earnestly to meditate on the law of God all day and all night, that is, at all times, he will not be victor over the aforesaid city. Whence the Psalmist: “Blessed,” he says, is the man “who meditates on the law of the Lord day and night, and hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, nor sat in the chair of pestilence.” But as to what it says, that they had previously put every male to the edge of the sword and rooted up the city, and so taken its spoils as they passed through the whole city over the slain, and then crossed the Jordan: it shows us that if we wish to be possessors of the law of the Lord, and to receive its spoils, that is, its various understandings, according to right faith, we should strive first to crush the surface of the letter, and to condemn all the errors of heretics. And so let us cross the Jordan into the great plain, that is, by the cleansing of baptism let us pass over into the liberty of glory, where the sun of justice may shine on us, in whose wings is true healing, who both enlightens the hidden things of darkness and reveals the secrets of mysteries, to those who seek him not with the pretence of feigning but with the truth of faith. Whence wisdom admonishes, saying: “Think of the Lord in goodness, and seek him in simplicity of heart; for he is found by them that tempt him not, and he sheweth himself to them that have faith in him. For perverse thoughts separate from God; but proved power reproveth the unwise. For wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul, nor dwell in a body subject to sins. For the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful, and will withdraw himself from thoughts that are without understanding.”
52_marg3802: And Judas was, etc. That Judas, returning with his army into the land of Juda, gathering the hindmost, “exhorted the people all the way through, till they came into the land of Juda,” instructs the teachers of holy Church by his example what care and what zeal they ought to have toward those under them: that on the way of the present life they not neglect to bestow on them the word of exhortation, but by teaching, admonishing, rebuking and consoling, they should always strive to profit them, and, as far as in them lies, allow no one to fall back from their company and perish. But rather let them hasten that, the number of those taken into their care being preserved, they may return glad into the land of Juda, according to the saying of Paul, to Mount Sion and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and the company of many thousands of angels, and “the church of the firstborn, who are written in the heavens, and to God the judge of all,” the Lord; and then give thanks with worthy praises to him by whose gift they will be able to come to the seat of rest and peace.
52_marg3803: And in the days when, etc. What is designated by these two leaders, Joseph namely and Azarias, who, provoked by emulation of the virtues of Judas, wished to acquire a name for themselves in battles through boasting, if not the person of hypocrites, who seek to imitate the virtues of the saints not with a simple intention but with the pride of arrogance. But as the things they did with no good spirit did not turn out prosperously for them, so for these too, from their endeavour there follows not true glory but everlasting ignominy, because they do not deserve to rejoice in the victory of their own, but rather will mourn over their own and their followers' perpetual damnation. Whence it is rightly added:
52_marg3804: And it was done, etc. Deservedly, then, he suffers the fall of a great slaughter who does not hear the wholesome counsel of the spiritual Judas, and because they were not of the number of the elect, who, stirred up by the Spirit of God, perform works of virtue, for their shameless boldness, shamefully confounded, they groan in the end with sinners.
52_marg3805: And the men of Juda, etc. It is well said that the men of Juda were magnified exceedingly in the sight of all nations, because those who hold the true confession of the right faith in such a way that they fulfil in works what they preach with the mouth are deservedly praised by the voice of all nations, and people come to them with joyful acclamations, that is, blessing them for their keeping of his commandments, they bring the praises of Juda to the heavenly king, according to that of the psalmist, who, considering the goods of the Church, says: “They have called the people happy, that hath these things: but happy is that people whose God is the Lord.” Hence also our Saviour in his Gospel commanded, saying: “So let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.”
52_marg3806: And Judas went forth. What is meant by Esau, who for greed of food sold his birthright to his younger brother Jacob, if not the former people, who by reason of earthly greed showed themselves unworthy of the honour of the firstborn, and for this reason the whole dignity was transferred to the people of the Gentiles? And well are the sons of Esau said to dwell in the land toward the south, because the Jewish people, on account of the law received and the writings of the prophets which were handed down to them, seemed to draw near to the light of the eternal sun. But because they were blinded in mind and placed beside the light, that very light “which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world,” they would not receive it set before them; hence they are plainly recorded as attacked by Judas and his brethren. For the holy teachers, reproaching them with their error, since they were justly despised and condemned for disobedience, turned to the preaching to the Gentiles, and, striking the error of the faithless, both in the synagogue itself and in individual persons, with the sword of the word of God, they burnt with the fire of deserved damnation the towers of pride which those men had raised with haughty mind against the Gospel of Christ.
52_marg3807: And he moved the camp. Note, reader, that he now recapitulates, touching briefly, all those kinds of adversaries which he had mentioned before, that is, of Jews, Gentiles and heretics. For when a little before he told that the sons of Esau were attacked, he soon added that the camp of the strangers was burnt together with the altars and the spoils of their gods. Then by the now travelled Samaria he recalls that not only Jewish superstition but also the error of the Gentiles and heretical wickedness, as the apostles preach, is overcome, confounded, destroyed and brought to nothing through the Gospel of Christ. Especially since “the lion of the tribe of Juda, the root of David, hath prevailed,” and who shall resist him? Judgment was hurled from heaven, the earth trembled and was still, “when God arose in judgment, to save all the meek of the earth.” But that among other things priests are said to have fallen in battle, while they went out to fight without counsel, is a sentence greatly to be feared, and care must be taken lest anyone, while he is intent on attacking the errors of others by his own wantonness and incautiousness, win for himself perpetual death.
52_marg3808: And king Antiochus. After the very many works of impiety which Antiochus did in the holy place and among the people of God, he was justly slain by divine judgment, as he himself testifies in what follows, saying that he knew that therefore these evils had found him, and thence he perished of grief in a strange land. Although Polybius of Megalopolis the historian, with Josephus as witness, writes that he perished because he wished to lay waste the temple of Diana in Persia, that is, in Elymais a city of the Persians. But this opinion is in no way received by the faithful, who know that “all the gods of the Gentiles are devils,” and that “the idols of the Gentiles are silver and gold, the works of the hands of men.” But because he swelled with pride against almighty God, he received fitting punishment. So also “all the wicked”; and likewise he who is last, “the son of perdition, who is lifted up above all that is called God or that is worshipped,” of whom this Antiochus was a type, because of the works of impiety which he did, would perish, visited by judgment from on high; whom the Lord Jesus, according to the word of Paul, “shall kill with the spirit of his mouth; and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming.”
52_marg3809: And he died. Whence he also holds the type of the persecutors of Christ and of the Church. It is no wonder that from a cruel father a savage son was begotten, who imitated the wicked works of a most wicked father. Of whom in the Gospel the Lord says to the cruel and proud Jews: “You are of your father the devil, and the desires of your father you will do. He was a murderer from the beginning.” And rightly the son of a murderer plans to commit murder, not only bodily but also spiritual, that is, the slaying of souls, which die in sin and impiety.
52_marg3810: And those who were. Who are those who shut up Israel in the citadel round about the saints, and always sought evils for them for the strengthening of the Gentiles, if not those who, raising themselves in the citadel of pride, persecute the true religion in the worshippers of Christ, so as to stifle the word of God and restore error and idolatry? Against these Judas arranges to fight, because the whole intention of the holy teachers is chiefly busied with this: that errors be overcome and those in error be conquered by the eminence of truth. But moved by this zeal, some of the Gentiles, such as the philosophers, and some also of the wicked of Israel, who are heretics, stir up the rule of this world to hatred of the servants of God, so that, helped by this support, they may more easily accomplish their impiety. Whence it is read that these, going to the king, said to him: How long will you not do judgment, and revenge our brethren? “We determined to serve thy father, and to do according to his orders, and obey his edicts: and the children of our people for this were alienated from us, and whosoever of us were found were slain, and our inheritances were spoiled, and they have not put forth their hand against us only, but also against all our borders.”
52_marg3811: And he was angry, etc. The typical Antiochus gathers an army not only from his own but also from foreigners, because the service of the persecutors, not content with internal sedition, stirs up huge wars against the servants of Christ even from outside. They set up foot soldiers, they array horsemen, they prepare elephants, so that nothing may be lacking to their cruelty, but whatever impiety can devise, savagery prepares it all. But figuratively, as the foot soldiers and horsemen can signify lictors and executioners, so also the elephants, on account of the enormity of their bodies and the cruelty of their minds, can signify the pride of princes; to whom it fits well that they showed the beasts “the blood of grapes, and mulberries” to provoke their anger, because in the shedding of the martyrs' blood the savagery of the persecutors was stirred up. And it is well said that “there stood by every elephant a thousand men in coats of mail, and with helmets on their heads, and horsemen set in order for every beast,” because there are many who favor the flattery of princes, whose coats of mail are linked together, that is, the wiles of wicked counsels are entangled with one another. And they have a helmet of brass on their heads, when they encircle their minds with the hardness of iniquity; where also horsemen are present in order, because the haughtiness of pride will not be lacking there, where the equality of the common nature is not considered through mercy, but the vanity of worldly favor is sought. But also the wooden towers, which, set upon the beasts, contained twenty-two men each, express the fragility of the power by which the persecutors always trust that they prevail over the martyrs. And it is rightly said: “Within was the master of the beast, and the rest of the horsemen he set on either side,” because the cruelty of minds, which was contriving all the evil, seethed within in the hearts of the persecutors, and the proud deeds also aided it from without in the torture of the innocent. And when these things were so arranged, Judas resolved to rouse his army with trumpets, because the holy preachers, when the wars of persecution press upon them, do not cease to strengthen the minds of their hearers with words. And although earthly glory shines in worldly pomp, or various kinds of tortures blaze in torments, yet the martyrs of Christ remain undaunted, and, clinging to the side of their spiritual avenger, they conquer and overthrow the boldness of the impious.
52_marg3812: And Eleazar saw, etc. It is to be noted that Josephus affirms this Eleazar to be the brother of Judas, of whom it was related above that he was one of the five sons of Matathias called by this name. But it can be asked how he is said to be the son of Saura, if he was the son of Matathias, unless perhaps Matathias himself was called Saura by another name. And what is signified by Eleazar, who died killing the elephant, if not the person of the arrogant, who, while they wish to do something bravely, yet not with a simple mind but a lofty one, are overcome and cast down in their endeavors. This matter can also, not unfittingly, be transferred to the signification of hypocrites. For when hypocrites fight by abstinence against lust, or gluttony, or bodily faults, and tame the flesh by fasting or by vigils and the other works of abstinence, yet do not guard themselves well against spiritual wickednesses, so that they do not beware of pride, or envy, or covetousness, they are as it were conquered by conquering, because while they overcome other vices, in the very victory they are heedlessly crushed by others.
52_marg3813: And they applied, etc. The mystical Antiochus moves his camp to Judea and Mount Sion, because he turns the whole apparatus of war to the overthrow of the Church of Christ; and he makes peace with those who were in Bethsura, since he offers not true peace but false to those whom he wishes to deceive and to beguile by pretense. But only those go out to him from the city who had no food while shut in; because only those, seduced, depart from the fortress of the Church who do not have the food of knowledge and charity, by which they may be fed in the soul. These also keep the sabbath badly, since they love not zeal for the virtues but the idleness of sloth. And they return by the enemy into captivity under his dominion, who are unwilling to guard against his snares. But that it is said the king turned his camp to the place of sanctification for many days, signifies that the persecutors of the faithful do not easily cease from the cruelty of persecution, but bring wars upon them all the days until the consummation of the world: for the testing of some believers, but for the deception of others. Because while the mystical woman, who was expressed by the figure of Eve, crushes the head of the serpent, the venomous snake itself will never cease to lie in wait for her heel. But what is added: “And there remained in the holy places but a few, for the famine had prevailed over them, and they were dispersed every man to his own place,” signifies that, when the persecution of unbelievers is raging, very many of those who persevered in the Church in appearance and not by constancy of faith are scattered for fear of punishments, according to what the Lord foretold in the Gospel for the last times to come: “For,” he says, there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people. “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword; and shall be led away captives into all nations; and Jerusalem shall be trodden down by the Gentiles; till the times of the nations be fulfilled.” “And unless those days had been shortened, no flesh should be saved: but for the sake of the elect those days shall be shortened.”
52_marg3814: And Lysias heard, etc. What Josephus relates hence seems not unworthy to be inserted in this work; nor should it seem burdensome to the reader if the narratives of different histories are compared with one another, because they seem to help each other in explaining the certainty of the matter and in setting forth again the truth of the history. Josephus narrates in this way: Lysias, the leader, and king Antiochus, when it was announced to them that Philip, coming from Persia, had presumed to seize the government committed to him, and wished to claim for himself the commonwealth of Antiochus, leaving off the siege, decreed to go against Philip. This counsel they would by no means make known to the other leaders; but the king ordered Lysias to tell the leaders that a long siege could profit them nothing, since it was agreed that the enemy’s place was fortified and a want of provisions was pressing upon them, and that it was expedient to make peace with the Jews, and to leave them to use their own ceremonies, on account of which, being hitherto forbidden by us, they seem to be our enemies. In saying this he decided that Philip’s tyranny should be passed over in silence, lest he perceive the wavering hearts of his army. When Lysias said this, the opinion pleased the army and the leaders. Then the king, sending to Judas, promised peace to the besieged, and pledged that they should live by their own laws. They, accepting the words, and the sacred rites and the pledge having been confirmed, went out from the temple. But Antiochus, entering and looking at the fortified place, shamelessly transgressed the oaths, and commanded the whole army standing round about to pull down the walls to the ground. After this he returned to Antioch, leading with him Onias, the chief of the priests, who was also called Menelaus. For Lysias persuaded the king to put Menelaus to death, if he wished the Jews to be at peace, saying that he had been the beginning of evils, who had persuaded his father to compel the Jews to leave their ancestral religion. The king therefore sending Menelaus to Beroea, a city of Syria, put him to death, in the tenth year of his priestly principate. And as he held the principate he drove the Jews to transgress the laws. After the death of Menelaus Alcimus, who was also called Joachim, was appointed prince. But king Antiochus, finding Philip ruling the state, made war on him, and having brought him under his power, killed him. The son of the high priest Onias, of whom we spoke before, was left a very little boy when his father died; and seeing that the king had killed his uncle Menelaus and had given the principate of the priesthood to Alcimus, who was not of the race of the priests, but had been swayed by Lysias so that in anger he might transfer the honour from that family to another house, he fled to Ptolemy king of Egypt, and obtained honour from him and from Cleopatra his wife, and asked a place in the region of Heliopolis, where he might build a temple like that of Jerusalem. But that Antiochus made a covenant with the Israelites, and swore to them, he and his princes, and yet did not keep the oath, but broke the oath and violated the pact, signifies that with heretics and unbelievers the agreement of a covenant will in no way be firm, because among them the observance of right is by no means fixed. Whence in no way is a covenant to be struck with vices and the author of vices, although they promise peace and feign prosperity, but at all times we must fight against them urgently with the shield of faith and the arms of justice. Then only must we cease from battle, when the enemy Antiochus no longer rages in the world, but is plunged and thrust down into hell.
52_marg3815: In the year one hundred, etc. “Demetrius the son of Seleucus departed from the city of Rome, and came up with a few men into a city of the sea coast, and reigned there,” etc. Of this Demetrius Pompeius Trogus in his history tells thus: When Antiochus departed, leaving a very small son, to whom guardians had been given by the people, his uncle Demetrius, who was a hostage at Rome, having learned of the death of his brother Antiochus, said that he had been born there, that he had come as a hostage while his brother lived, and that, he being dead, he did not know whose hostage he was. It was therefore just that he be sent away to seek the kingdom, because as by the law of nations it had yielded to the elder brother, so now it was due to himself, who was older than the ward. When he perceived that he was not being sent away by the senate, which by a silent judgment thought that the kingdom would be safer with the ward than with him, he set out from the city under pretence of hunting, and silently with the companions of his flight boarded a ship. Brought to Syria, he was received with the favour of all, and, the ward having been killed by the guardians, the kingdom was handed over to him.
52_marg3816: And there came, etc. What is signified by king Demetrius, but the princes of the Gentiles who stir up persecution against the Church of Christ? The interpretation of the name explains this well. For it is interpreted vehemently inveighing, or exceedingly persecuting. To this prince therefore come “the wicked and ungodly men of Israel,” and Alcimus their leader, like those who, after the faith of Christ was received, returned to apostasy, blaspheme the Christian religion and disparage the worship of the Church; their leaders are heretics, who through ambition of loftiness wish to seem great to all. But this ruin having been received, Demetrius typically sends Bacchides, who ruled beyond the river in the kingdom, to establish the wicked Alcimus in the priesthood, and to take vengeance on the children of Israel. When the heretic offers the support of his pride through any pagans powerful in the world, who have not yet deserved to be dipped in the baptism of Christ and to be counted in the number of the faithful, he also inflicts the torture of torments on the true confessors of Christ. But although such persons speak peaceful words in guile to Judas and his brethren, yet they pay no heed to their speeches, because they in no way consent to their perfidy.
52_marg3817: And Alcimus saw Judas. Who is Judas, who takes vengeance on the transgressors, but our Redeemer, who avenges his elect, and permits none of his own to perish in vain? But he exercises vengeance on those who deserve it in two ways. Some, calling them from the fountain of his great mercy to repentance of their error, he makes to rise up against themselves, that they may punish with lamentations what they did in wicked deeds. Others, by a just judgment after crimes committed, he lets continue uncorrected in their hardness, that afterwards he may bestow on them the worthy punishments which they deserved by their wicked works.
52_marg3818: And the king sent, etc. By Nicanor the just, whom we read in another place to have been set over the elephants, we can understand false apostles or pseudo-prophets, who, of the Jews, intent on the exercise of their pride, came to the Church of the Gentiles. These, striving by pretence to bring error into the Church of Christ, feigned themselves to be peaceable, but, as will appear in the end, were most savage enemies. Of whom the apostle John, writing in his Apocalypse, says: “Who say they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan”; whom the teacher of the Gentiles in his epistle calls false apostles, deceitful workers, who transform themselves into apostles of Christ; and no wonder, since Satan himself transformeth himself into an angel of light. Whence it is no great thing if his ministers be transformed as the ministers of justice, whose end shall be according to their works. These therefore, like Nicanor, stretching out the hand against the temple of the Lord, blaspheme; because they detract from the power of Christ, who is in the Church, as if less able, saying to the brethren: “Unless you be circumcised after the manner of Moses, you cannot be saved”; for so it is read that they taught in the Acts of the Apostles; but when victory has been gained through our Judas and his companions, the blasphemous head of this error is cut off together with Nicanor, and the right hand of the wicked action, lest any further injury of such blasphemy be inflicted on the divine majesty. For the apostle Paul says to us: “By grace you are saved through faith, and that not of yourselves, for it is the gift of God; not of works, that no man may glory. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus in good works, which God hath prepared that we should walk in them.”
52_marg3819: And Judas chose. Judas, who sends ambassadors to the Romans to make with them friendship and alliance, signifies our Redeemer offering through holy preachers the Gospel of peace to the Gentiles and calling them together to his faith. To whom they wrote back on tables of brass what had been asked of them, and sent it to Jerusalem, that there it might be with them a memorial of peace and alliance; because the Gentiles converted to belief in Christ establish a firm covenant of their faith, which they mark as one to last a long time, and hand down a monument of true confession in the Catholic Church, that there it may be a memorial of their fellowship for ever. Whence it is said through the prophet: “Behold, the Lord hath made himself heard, and hath sent ambassadors to the Gentiles; and the angel of his face shall save them; in his love and in his mercy he redeemed them.” And likewise: “It is a small thing,” he says, “that thou shouldst be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to convert the dregs of Israel. Behold, I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth.” And again: “I have given thee to be a covenant of the people, that thou mightest raise up the earth, and possess the inheritances that were destroyed.” And what is the meaning that Judas sent two ambassadors to the Romans for the sake of making peace, unless that our Redeemer, to call the Gentiles together to the faith and fellowship of peace, sent the two testaments into the world; or otherwise he sends messengers two by two because of the sacrament of charity, since there are two precepts of charity, that is, of the love of God and of neighbour, and all charity cannot be had among fewer than two. For no one is properly said to have charity toward himself, but by love he reaches out toward another, that there may be charity. The Lord sends the disciples two and two to preach in the Gospel, that he may silently hint this to us, that he who has not charity toward another ought by no means to take up the office of preaching. And it is well said that “he sent them two and two before his face into every city and place whither he himself was to come.” For the Lord follows his preachers, because preaching goes before, and then the Lord comes to the dwelling of our mind, the words of exhortation run before, and through this the truth is received in the mind.
52_marg3820: In the mean time again, etc. Demetrius renews the war again through Bacchides and Alcimus against Judas, because through pagans and heretics fallen back from the faith of Christ the prince of the world every day renews against the Church old snares with new arts to do harm; with whom also he sent the right wing, when for the perpetration of such wickedness he supplies a strong band of helpers. Against whom Judas goes with three thousand, because against all the enemies of the faith he arranges that the company of teachers fight with the faithful, that through the faith of the holy Trinity he may lay low the host of the enemy, which in vain presumption, being proud, dares to raise itself against its own author. But let us see what follows next in the writing.
52_marg3821: And many saw, etc. Because although many seem to remain in the confession of the Catholic faith, yet when persecution blazes up it will appear who were fixed in the faith and who seemed to be in it only in appearance. Whence it is written in the Gospel parable that when the sun was risen the crops withered which had been on stony ground and had not had much earth. Because those who hold no firm roots of belief in the heart, believing for a time, fall away in time of temptation. Of the three thousand therefore there remained with Judas only eight hundred men; because when the reprobate fall away from the fellowship of the Church, only the elect, who are predestined to receive eternal blessedness, will remain in the stability of sound faith.
52_marg3822: And the army moved, etc. What is the meaning that when the army was moved from the camp the horsemen are told to have been divided into two parts, unless that among the proud and arrogant unity and firm concord can never be kept, as the Scripture bears witness, which says: “Among the proud there are always contentions.” And the slingers, it says, and the archers went before the army. What is meant by slingers and archers, unless those who desire either to allure the minds of men to idolatry or apostasy, or by flattering with vain promises of prosperity, as by the whirling of a sling, to pervert the faithful, or strive to deceive them by terrifying them with threats of torments, as with the strokes of arrows. And fittingly these are described as going before the army, because it has always been the custom of persecutors to anticipate the exacting of torments by such devices.
52_marg3823: And it was moved, etc. The earth, he says, was moved by the voice of the armies; that is, the hearts of the carnal were shaken with fear of persecutions. And the battle was fought from morning even unto the evening. For from the rising of the dawning faith even to the end of the world, the camps of the devil cease not to fight against the Church of God, and never leave off stirring up the adversities of tribulations against the good. These, according to the saying of Paul: “All that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.” Judas saw that the stronger part of the army of Bacchides was on the right, and, having gathered to himself all that were steadfast, he discomfited it in heart. While the holy teachers, with the fitting consolations of the faithful joined together, strive to overcome the assault of the Gentiles by the word of faith and to bring them to the tranquillity of faith. For their part seemed the stronger, because openly, in pagan error, through the cruelty of tortures they raged against the Church, rather than those who with feigned friendships craftily laid snares for the brethren. But Judas pursues the army of Bacchides even to the end of Azotus, when the preachers of the Gospel strive to bring the fury of the Gentiles to the fire of pious love. For Azotus is interpreted the fire of a paternal uncle. That love can be said to be the one which burned in the hearts of the patriarchs, which the vigor of the teachers desires to form in the minds of the sons, that what is written of Elias may be fulfilled: “That he may turn the hearts of the fathers unto the children, and the incredulous to the wisdom of the just, to prepare unto the Lord a perfect people.”
52_marg3824: And those on the left. The right wing, which was the stronger, having fallen, the left wing pursues Judas from behind; because, the heavy persecution of the Gentiles being in a way lulled, the heretics with a left-handed intention cease not at all to pursue the holy Church, craftily lying in wait and secretly wounding her as it were from behind. Hence follows:
52_marg3825: And Judas was slain, etc. Because, when the shepherds are slain, the flocks are forced to flee in different directions, as it is written in the prophet Zacharias, in foreshadowing the passion of Christ: “Strike,” he says, “the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be dispersed.” The Evangelist brought this in as testimony in the passion of the Lord, where, when he was seized by the crowds, “the disciples all leaving him, fled.” For what went before in the head must needs follow in the body.
52_marg3826: And Jonathan and. The ruin of good masters by the setting of temporal death cannot pass without the sadness of the disciples. Hence it is said that all the people of Israel bewailed Judas with great lamentation. A like thing is found written in the passion of Stephen: that “devout men took order for Stephen’s funeral, and made great mourning over him.” But though grief at the departure of their own touches the minds of the faithful through compassion, yet they will not lack the consolation which they have through sure hope of the future rest of souls. For the saints are in some way saddened in the sorrow of their body, but are exceedingly glad in spirit for the reward assigned to them in the heavenly kingdom. Whence the Saviour, foretelling to his disciples in the Gospel the greatness of the passion and the sure recompense of his triumph, says: “Blessed are ye when they shall revile you, and persecute you, and speak all that is evil against you, untruly, for my sake. Be glad in that day and rejoice; for behold, your reward is great in heaven.”
52_marg3827: And the rest of the words. Many are the wars and mighty works that the saints do, or rather the Lord in them, the knowledge of all which no one can grasp. But they remain only in the knowledge of their author. Whence the Lord says of them in the Gospel: “My sheep hear my voice, and I the Lord know them.” And again: “Be glad,” he says, “and rejoice, for your names are written in heaven.” And again: “Your hairs,” he says, “of your head are all numbered, and a hair of your head shall not perish.” Of which it is written elsewhere: “The Lord knoweth who are his.” And again: “He alone knoweth the hearts of all the children of Adam.” Hence in the Psalm the prophet says: “Who telleth the number of the stars: and calleth them all by their names.” And again: “God,” he says, “is wonderful in his saints. He will give power and strength to his people.” Whence it is necessary that each one say, and all say: “Blessed be God, who alone doth wonderful things,” and “blessed be the name of his majesty for ever and ever.”
52_marg3828: And it came to pass after. In the earlier part, where the death of Mathathias is recorded, it is found written that he died in the hundred and forty-sixth year. In his place rose up Judas his son, and fought the battle of Israel. Likewise in what follows it is found written that Jonathan took the leadership after Judas his brother. After him Alcimus, in the hundred and fifty-third year, commanded the walls of the holy house and the works of the prophets to be destroyed, and he died at that time. But Josephus relates that after Alcimus, who was also called Joachim, had held the principate of the priesthood four years and died, the people handed the priesthood over to Judas; and he says that Judas, after he had ministered in the principate of the priesthood three years, died. From all this it may be gathered that Judas, after the death of Mathathias his father, held the leadership of the people seven years; in which, for a space of four years, driving the generals of Antiochus out of Judea by fighting, and cleansing the temple of the images of the idols, he afterwards restored the ancestral laws to his citizens, in the hundred and fifty-fourth Olympiad; and so he received the principate of the priesthood and fulfilled three years in it. Whence also in the chronicles it is found that Jonathan received the leadership of the Jews in the sixth year of Demetrius Soter, which he held nineteen years, that is, ten years after the death of his father Mathathias, in the hundred and fifty-fifth Olympiad. That harassment of the wicked, then, which after the death of Judas troubled the children of Israel, signifies mystically that when good teachers are taken away, the faithful hearers feel no small loss, since, the occasion being seized, not only pagans but also heretics weary the Church of God with grievous persecutions.
